speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to help me understand your condition, how long has this rash been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash has persisted for 5 months without complete resolution despite occasional worsening. Do you notice any specific pattern to the rash, such as it appearing only after exposure to heat, sunlight, or certain fabrics?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Polymorphous Light Eruption (PMLE).

The chronic nature (5 months), bilateral upper extremity distribution, pruritus, and lack of systemic symptoms like fever or joint pain strongly suggest a photosensitive reaction. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of the rash to look for follicular-centric edema and vesicles typical of PMLE.
